proposals.before: Consorts and attendants now filled the palace, and Lady Cao seldom gained access to the emperor's bedchamber, yet the empress dowager's favor toward her never diminished.
proposals.after: Consorts and attendants now filled the palace, and Lady Cao seldom gained access to the emperor's bedchamber, yet imperial favor toward her never diminished.
proposals.reason: 太后 here is Cao, the biographical subject, not a third party conferring favor; 恩顧 is continuing imperial favor toward her.

proposals.before: At that time consorts and attendants filled the chambers, and Lady Cao rarely gained access to the imperial bed, yet the Empress Dowager's gracious favor toward her never waned.
proposals.after: At that time consorts and attendants filled the chambers, and she rarely gained access to the imperial bed, yet gracious favor toward the Empress Dowager never waned.
proposals.reason: The rest of this biography uses 太后 for Cao; the English third-party reading reverses the referent.

proposals.before: She then said to Emperor Zhuangzong, "The Grand Consort and I are as close as elder and younger brother. She has been ill for years; if she could only see my face, that would be enough to comfort her heart. I shall go briefly to Jinyang and return with her within a month."
proposals.after: She then said to Emperor Zhuangzong, "The Grand Consort and I are as close as elder and younger siblings. She has been ill for years; if she could only see my face, that would be enough to comfort her heart. I shall go briefly to Jinyang and return with her within a month."
proposals.reason: 伯仲 is sibling closeness; brother missexes the two women.

proposals.before: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the fourth month of the first year of Tongguang she was enfeoffed as imperial grand consort.
proposals.after: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the fourth month of the first year of Tongguang she was invested as imperial grand consort.
proposals.reason: 冊為 is ceremonial investiture of a consort title, not a territorial enfeoffment.

proposals.before: The 《History of Ouyang》 records that when Zhuangzong took the throne, he enfeoffed Lady Cao as empress dowager and made his principal mother Lady Liu imperial grand consort.
proposals.after: The 《History of Ouyang》 records that when Zhuangzong took the throne, he invested and honored Lady Cao as empress dowager and made his principal mother Lady Liu imperial grand consort.
proposals.reason: 冊尊 is investiture and honoring of court titles, not enfeoffment with land.

proposals.before: During the Tiancheng era, Emperor Ming visited her monastery and changed her grant to Great Master Yuanhui.
proposals.after: During the Tiancheng era, Emperor Mingzong visited her monastery and changed her grant to Great Master Yuanhui.

proposals.before: When Li Keyong attacked Weizhou and took Cheng'an, he obtained the future empress, who was then five or six years old.

proposals.reason: Chinese names the attacker only as 太祖; the idiomatic English inserts the personal name Li Keyong, which is not in this sentence.

proposals.after: We have also reviewed the national histories and observe that the mother of Emperor Xuanzong was Empress Zhaocheng Dou, and the mother of Emperor Daizong was Empress Dowager Zhangjing Wu. proposals.reason: 俄幽宮 here means the consorts soon died and were laid in the palace, not that they were imprisoned; the memorial's point is posthumous honor after early death.

decisions.reason: 太后 is Cao herself, the biography’s subject; 唯太后恩顧不衰 means imperial favor toward her never waned, not favor conferred by a third-party empress dowager.
The same clause makes Cao (太后) the recipient of 恩顧, matching later units where 太后 is Cao; the original English treats the title as a separate person conferring favor.

decisions.reason: 伯仲 is a sibling-closeness metaphor; both speakers are women, so “brother” missexes them.
冊為皇太妃 is ceremonial investiture of a court title, not a territorial enfeoffment.
冊尊曹氏為皇太后 is investiture and honoring of a title; “enfeoffed” misstates 冊尊.
）〉 closes the editorial note and is not part of the sentence 太妃薨.
天成中，明帝 is Later Tang Mingzong, not an unspecified Emperor Ming; the idiomatic field already has Mingzong.
Idiomatic English may identify 太祖 as Li Keyong; that naming is historically accurate, and the literal field already keeps Founding Emperor. The change is a calque preference, not a semantic error.
請冊劉氏為皇后 is a request to invest her as empress, not to enfeoff a fief.
同光二年十二月冊 and the following 冊使/受冊 describe consort investiture, not enfeoffment.
冊使 and 受冊於內 are investiture commissioners and receipt of the patent, not enfeoffment.
